title: Rational Equations and Inverse Variation
seo_title: Algebra II Rational Equations and Inverse Variation Worksheets (TEKS 2A.6H–2A.6L)
domain: Cubic, Cube Root, Absolute Value, and Rational Functions, Equations, and Inequalities
standard_text: 2A.6H formulate rational equations that model real-world situations; 2A.6I solve rational equations that have real solutions; 2A.6J determine the reasonableness of a solution to a rational equation; 2A.6L formulate and solve equations involving inverse variation
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.6H to 2A.6L: solve rational equations, extraneous solutions, work and rate problems, and inverse variation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply by the LCD, solve, and check for extraneous solutions.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To solve a rational equation, multiply both sides by the least common denominator. Then solve.
  • Check: a value that makes any denominator 0 is extraneous.
  • Work problems: rates add. If one person takes 3 hours, the rate is 13 job per hour.
  • Inverse variation: y = kx, so xy = k. As one goes up, the other goes down.

Examples

Example

y = 8 when x = 3; find y when x = 6

k = 3 × 8 = 24

24 ÷ 6 = 4

Answer: y = 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Keeping a value that makes a denominator 0Check every answer in the original equation.
Adding times instead of ratesAdd 1/3 + 1/6, not 3 + 6.
Using direct variationInverse: multiply x and y to get k.

faq.a: Formulate rational equations that model real-world situations.
Solve rational equations that have real solutions, and determine the reasonableness of a solution to a rational equation.
Formulate and solve equations involving inverse variation.

faq.q: What does the graph of an inverse variation look like?
faq.a: A curve like y = k/x with asymptotes on both axes.

items.q: Solve 5x − 3 = 25x + 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 5(x + 1) = 25(x − 3). Then 5x + 5 = 25x − 75, so x = 4. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 7x − 6 = −42x + 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 7(x + 1) = −42(x − 6). Then 7x + 7 = −42x + 252, so x = 5. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 2x − 6 = −4x − 3.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 2(x − 3) = −4(x − 6). Then 2x − 6 = −4x + 24, so x = 5. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 6x + 3 = 14x − 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 6(x − 1) = 14(x + 3). Then 6x − 6 = 14x + 42, so x = −6. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 6x + 3 = 2x − 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 6(x − 1) = 2(x + 3). Then 6x − 6 = 2x + 6, so x = 3. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x − 6 = 1x + 3.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 4(x + 3) = 1(x − 6). Then 4x + 12 = 1x − 6, so x = −6. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 5x − 6 = −25x + 6.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 5(x + 6) = −25(x − 6). Then 5x + 30 = −25x + 150, so x = 4. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x + 5 = −12x + 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 4(x + 1) = −12(x + 5). Then 4x + 4 = −12x − 60, so x = −4. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 3x − 5 = −3x + 1.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 3(x + 1) = −3(x − 5). Then 3x + 3 = −3x + 15, so x = 2. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x + 1 = −4x − 5.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 4(x − 5) = −4(x + 1). Then 4x − 20 = −4x − 4, so x = 2. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x + 4 = 24x − 6.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 4(x − 6) = 24(x + 4). Then 4x − 24 = 24x + 96, so x = −6. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 4x − 2 = −2x + 4.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 4(x + 4) = −2(x − 2). Then 4x + 16 = −2x + 4, so x = −2. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 5x − 4 = 20x + 2.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 5(x + 2) = 20(x − 4). Then 5x + 10 = 20x − 80, so x = 6. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 2x − 3 = −1x + 6.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 2(x + 6) = −1(x − 3). Then 2x + 12 = −1x + 3, so x = −3. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 7x + 2 = −21x + 6.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 7(x + 6) = −21(x + 2). Then 7x + 42 = −21x − 42, so x = −3. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 2x + 5 = 10x − 3.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 2(x − 3) = 10(x + 5). Then 2x − 6 = 10x + 50, so x = −7. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 3x − 4 = 5x − 6.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 3(x − 6) = 5(x − 4). Then 3x − 18 = 5x − 20, so x = 1. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 6x + 6 = 33x − 3.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 6(x − 3) = 33(x + 6). Then 6x − 18 = 33x + 198, so x = −8. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 2x − 2 = −10x + 4.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 2(x + 4) = −10(x − 2). Then 2x + 8 = −10x + 20, so x = 1. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve 3x − 2 = 2x − 4.
items.e: Cross-multiply: 3(x − 4) = 2(x − 2). Then 3x − 12 = 2x − 4, so x = 8. Check: it does not make a denominator 0.

items.q: Solve x²x − 5 = x + 20x − 5.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 5): x² = x + 20, so (x + 4)(x − 5) = 0 and x = 5 or −4. But x = 5 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −4.

items.q: Solve x²x − 2 = 3x − 2x − 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 2): x² = 3x − 2, so (x − 1)(x − 2) = 0 and x = 2 or 1. But x = 2 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 1.

items.q: Solve x²x − 4 = 4xx − 4.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 4): x² = 4x, so x(x − 4) = 0 and x = 4 or 0. But x = 4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 0.

items.q: Solve x + 12x = −7.
items.e: Multiply by x: x² + 7x + 12 = 0, so (x + 4)(x + 3) = 0. Neither solution is 0, so both work. x = −4, −3.

items.q: Solve x − 24x = 2.
items.e: Multiply by x: x² − 2x − 24 = 0, so (x − 6)(x + 4) = 0. Neither solution is 0, so both work. x = −4, 6.

items.q: Solve x²x − 4 = x + 12x − 4.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 4): x² = x + 12, so (x + 3)(x − 4) = 0 and x = 4 or −3. But x = 4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −3.

items.q: Solve x²x − 1 = −x + 2x − 1.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 1): x² = −x + 2, so (x + 2)(x − 1) = 0 and x = 1 or −2. But x = 1 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −2.

items.q: Solve 16 + 1x = 14.
items.e: 1x = 14 − 16 = 112, so x = 12. (Subtracting denominators, 6 − 4, is a common mistake.)

items.q: Solve x²x − 2 = 2xx − 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 2): x² = 2x, so x(x − 2) = 0 and x = 2 or 0. But x = 2 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 0.

items.q: Solve x²x − 1 = 5x − 4x − 1.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 1): x² = 5x − 4, so (x − 4)(x − 1) = 0 and x = 1 or 4. But x = 1 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 4.

items.q: Solve x²x + 2 = 4x + 12x + 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 2): x² = 4x + 12, so (x − 6)(x + 2) = 0 and x = −2 or 6. But x = −2 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 6.

items.q: Solve x²x + 4 = −3x + 4x + 4.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 4): x² = −3x + 4, so (x − 1)(x + 4) = 0 and x = −4 or 1. But x = −4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 1.

items.q: Solve x − 20x = 1.
items.e: Multiply by x: x² − x − 20 = 0, so (x + 4)(x − 5) = 0. Neither solution is 0, so both work. x = −4, 5.

items.q: Solve x²x + 5 = 25x + 5.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 5): x² = 25, so (x − 5)(x + 5) = 0 and x = −5 or 5. But x = −5 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 5.

items.q: Solve x²x + 4 = −5x − 4x + 4.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 4): x² = −5x − 4, so (x + 1)(x + 4) = 0 and x = −4 or −1. But x = −4 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −1.

items.q: Solve x + 4x = 5.
items.e: Multiply by x: x² − 5x + 4 = 0, so (x − 1)(x − 4) = 0. Neither solution is 0, so both work. x = 1, 4.

items.q: Solve x²x + 3 = −7x − 12x + 3.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 3): x² = −7x − 12, so (x + 4)(x + 3) = 0 and x = −3 or −4. But x = −3 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −4.

items.q: Solve x²x + 5 = −11x − 30x + 5.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 5): x² = −11x − 30, so (x + 6)(x + 5) = 0 and x = −5 or −6. But x = −5 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −6.

items.q: Solve x²x − 2 = x + 2x − 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 2): x² = x + 2, so (x + 1)(x − 2) = 0 and x = 2 or −1. But x = 2 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = −1.

items.q: Solve x²x + 2 = −x + 2x + 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 2): x² = −x + 2, so (x − 1)(x + 2) = 0 and x = −2 or 1. But x = −2 makes the denominator 0, so it is extraneous. x = 1.

items.q: Valeria can paint a fence in 3 hours, and Nevaeh can paint it in 6 hours. How long will it take them working together?
items.e: Add the rates: 13 + 16 = 1x, which is 12 of the job per hour. Time = 1 ÷ 12 = 2 hours.

items.q: A boat travels 80 miles downstream in the same time it travels 40 miles upstream. The current is 5 mph. What is the boat's speed in still water?
items.e: Same time: 80r + 5 = 40r − 5. Cross-multiply and solve: r = 15 mph.

items.q: y varies inversely with x, and y = 15 when x = 3. What is the constant of variation k?
items.e: Inverse variation: xy = k. k = 3 × 15 = 45.

items.q: y varies inversely with x, and y = 5 when x = 10. Write the equation.
